h1: Wordless picture books for the classroom
lead: Every child can join in, whatever language they speak at home.
intro: Telning books have no words, so the whole class can tell the story together. One picture per page, one change per page, and a fork with two endings to talk about. This page shows how teachers use them with a whole class, a small group, or one child.

why.h2: Why do wordless books work in class?

cards.t: No reading level, no language barrier. A child who speaks Arabic at home and a child who speaks Swedish tell the same page.
With wordless books, adults ask more open questions and children say more. The book is the stage; the talk is the play.
Simple pages keep attention on the story. Children with less language can still follow and take part.
Two endings side by side. Half the class picks one, half the other. Then: why?

why.therapists: Speech therapists often use wordless books to get children telling stories. The same clear sequence works for a class.

how.lead: The same four steps as at home: Talk, Ask, Decide, Act. Three ways to run them.

modes.t: Show one page at a time on the screen or hold the book up. Ask one question per page and take three answers. At the fork, vote with hands, then ask two children why.
Four to six children, one book. Each child tells one page in turn. The group chooses the ending together and has to agree on a reason.
The child holds the book and tells the whole story. You ask, wait, and add one word. Good for a child who is new to the language of the classroom.

topics.h2: Topics you can teach with the books
topics.lead: Feelings and life skills, in the words children use. In teacher language: SEL.

items.t: Naming a feeling, seeing it in a face and a body, noticing it change.
Sharing, taking turns, joining a game, saying sorry.
Seeing two ways, thinking about what happens next, picking one and saying why.
A new place, a first day, a visit to the doctor, bedtime.
